_description: Latency budgets for the two lanes ADR-058 D6 hard-gates. This is the ONLY checked-in source of these numbers — scripts/qe/card-lane-gate.mjs and scripts/qe/session-start-gate.mjs read them at runtime and enforce them as HARD entries inside scripts/qe/ux-suite.mjs. docs/adr/0058-the-95-contract.md `governs:` this file, so a threshold edit here that is not accompanied by a currency-log entry on that ADR shows up as governed-set drift under `node scripts/doc-currency.mjs --check` — a silent raise is itself a gate failure, not a free edit. The card-lane keys stay at the TOP LEVEL (unchanged shape, unchanged reader); the second lane lives under `sessionStart`.
_secondLane: WHY A SECOND ROW EXISTS (2026-07-28, closing a named grading deduction): the top-level card-lane row measures a 0.03–0.22ms in-process function against a 250ms budget. That is ~1,000x headroom BY DESIGN — see scripts/qe/card-lane-gate.mjs's header — and the honest consequence, stated by an independent grader, is that it can only catch catastrophic regression classes while everything the user actually FEELS stayed advisory or unmeasured. `sessionStart` below is the first user-felt number promoted to a hard gate: the wall time of the SessionStart hook a stranger's Claude Code fires before their first prompt is answered. It is measured through the REAL registered command by the watchdog scripts/selfcheck.mjs already ships — not by a second, hand-rolled timer.

measuredBaseline.note: Hand-measured before this gate existed (see ADR-058's scoreboard row 'Fast lane'). The gate itself re-measures p50/p95/max on every run rather than trusting these — this block is provenance, never an input to pass/fail.

justification: absoluteFailMs=1000 is ~8,600x the measured 0.1158ms warm baseline, so a breach there is a correctness event (something is genuinely blocking, e.g. a stray await/sleep or a hung fs call), not scheduler jitter — which is exactly why hard-gating it does not violate scripts/qe/ux-suite.mjs's own anti-flake rule for the environment-sensitive timings. The number itself is not arbitrary: every hook in plugin/hooks/hooks.json carries a 5s timeout, and those hooks order the model to consult search_ruvnet before writing — a product may not order a consultation it prices above its own intervention budget. p95BudgetMs=250 is the everyday target with ~2,159x headroom over the measured baseline; breaching only the 250ms budget (without crossing 1000ms) is still a hard FAIL under this gate, since D6 promotes the whole deterministic decision lane to a hard gate rather than leaving it advisory.
measurementMethod: IN-PROCESS function calls only (no subprocess per firing) — see scripts/qe/card-lane-gate.mjs header. A GitHub ubuntu CI runner has 2 vCPU vs this dev machine's 16; subprocess-per-firing measurement has already produced starved, empty-looking output on that runner twice. Measuring in-process means the number reflects kb/card-lane.mjs itself, not the OS scheduler.

sessionStart._description: SESSION-START WALL TIME — the first user-felt number in this repo to become a hard gate. Enforced by scripts/qe/session-start-gate.mjs, wired as a HARD entry in scripts/qe/ux-suite.mjs beside the card lane. Every firing is the LITERAL registered command from plugin/hooks/hooks.json (`node hook-shim.mjs session-start`), fired through scripts/selfcheck.mjs's existing external process-group watchdog — the same door a stranger's Claude Code uses. Nothing here re-implements a timer: fireHook() already returns elapsedMs and already enforces the declared timeout.

measuredBaseline.runs: three sequential runs of n=30 / n=30 / n=50 in three separate virgin HOMEs, one untimed warm-up fire each. Per-run p95: 276 / 225 / 323 ms. Per-run max: 374 / 283 / 440 ms.
measuredBaseline.note: Provenance, never an input to pass/fail — the gate re-measures p50/p95/max on every run. Recorded so the budget below can be checked against the evidence that set it instead of being taken on trust.

sessionStart.justification: p95BudgetMs=1000 is ~3.1x the WORST measured p95 (323ms) and ~2.3x the worst single sample (440ms) — deliberately NOT the ~1,000x of the row above, because ~1,000x headroom is exactly the deduction this row exists to close. The 3x factor is not a comfort margin, it is the platform gap: a GitHub ubuntu-latest runner has 2 vCPU against this machine's 16 (.github/workflows/ci.yml states this in its own header and sizes every timeout for it), and unlike the card lane every firing here is a real fork/exec of bash + node, so the scheduler IS part of the measurement and cannot be factored out. absoluteFailMs=4000 is not a chosen number at all: it is TIMEOUT_MARGIN (0.8) x the 5s timeout the SessionStart registration declares for itself in plugin/hooks/hooks.json, i.e. the exact wall scripts/selfcheck.mjs's assertContract() already enforces on a stranger's machine. Past it the hook has no margin left inside its own registered timeout, and a user is waiting on it before their first prompt is answered. Breaching only p95BudgetMs (without reaching absoluteFailMs) is still a HARD FAIL, matching the card lane's semantics one row up.
sessionStart.measurementMethod: SUBPROCESS PER FIRING, unavoidably and correctly — the thing under measurement IS a subprocess, so the in-process rule stated for the card lane does not transfer. Consequences, handled rather than ignored: (1) the gate fires against the CHECKOUT's plugin/ tree (resolveInstalledSurface is given a fresh empty HOME so the developer's own possibly-stale ~/.claude/plugins cache can never be the thing measured); (2) HOME is a fresh temp dir per run, so the hook never reads or writes the developer's real state; (3) ONE untimed warm-up fire precedes the timed samples, because the first-ever fire in a virgin HOME additionally emits the once-per-machine offers — the timed window is the STEADY STATE every session after the first, which is the common case and the reproducible one; (4) samples are sequential, never concurrent, so the number is one hook's cost and not a measure of how many cores the runner has.
